ctx: A bakery assistant has the system message "You are helpful." Customers ask it for homework help and for medical advice, and it answers. The owner wants answers about cakes and orders only.
q: Which change should the owner make first?
opts: State the scope and how to decline other topics
Add the sentence "You are very, very helpful and never make mistakes"
Deploy the same model again in a second region
Ask customers to write shorter questions
exp: A clear scope with instructions for out-of-scope questions is the direct way to limit an assistant. Praise in the prompt does not set limits, a second region runs the same behavior, and short questions can still be off topic.

ctx: A team turns emails into JSON with the keys customer, product and urgency. With instructions only, 8 of 100 answers use other key names. With three example pairs in the prompt, 1 of 100 does. Any wrong key stops the program.
q: What should the team do next?
opts: Accept the result, because 1% is normal
Use structured outputs with a JSON schema
Write the instructions in capital letters and repeat each of them
Raise the temperature
exp: Structured outputs constrain the reply to the schema, so key names cannot vary. Examples lower the error rate but give no guarantee, capitals and repetition give none either, and a higher temperature makes the output vary more.

ctx: A tutor app sends this system message with every request: "Explain in simple words. Ask one question back. If you are not sure, say so." Each user message holds the question of the student.
q: For each of the following statements about this scenario, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: The system message sets the tone for all students.
The system message guarantees that no answer is wrong.
The question of the student belongs in the system message.
exp: Yes for the first: the system message is the same in every request. No for the second: it guides the model but cannot guarantee correct answers. No for the third: the changing question is the user message, and the system message holds lasting instructions.

ctx: A team wants to choose between three models for a contract assistant. It has 150 real questions with approved answers and needs numbers that a manager can compare.
q: What should the team do in the Foundry portal?
opts: Ask each model in the playground which of the three is best
Run an evaluation of the models on the 150 questions
Choose the newest model
Compare the number of characters in the names of the deployments
exp: An evaluation runs the same data through each model and reports quality and safety metrics that can be compared. A model cannot judge itself reliably, the newest model is not always the best for a task, and names say nothing about quality.

ctx: An internal app works well for 30 employees. On Monday it is opened to 2,000 employees, and about half of the calls return HTTP 429. Answers that arrive are still correct.
q: What is the most likely fix?
opts: Increase the tokens-per-minute capacity of the deployment
Shorten the system message so that it has no examples and no rules left in it
Fine-tune the model on the questions from Monday
Turn off the content filter
exp: HTTP 429 means that a rate limit was reached, and the load grew by a factor of about 60, so the deployment needs more quota or another capacity type. Fine-tuning and filters change answers and not limits, and a shorter system message gives up quality for a small saving.

ctx: A children's reading app uses a deployed chat model. The owner must block violent content in both directions, stop attempts to bypass the rules and never mention a list of competitor names.
q: Which THREE guardrail settings meet the requirements? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opts: A strict violence filter for input and output
Prompt Shields for user prompts
A higher value for the top_p setting of the deployment
A blocklist with the competitor names
A second deployment of the same model in a different region
exp: The violence filter handles harmful content on both sides, Prompt Shields detect jailbreak attempts, and a blocklist stops exact terms. top_p changes how words are sampled, and a second deployment repeats the same behavior elsewhere.

ctx: A developer tests a chat client with an endpoint copied from an old tutorial. The portal shows the project endpoint https://contoso.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/support, and the client uses https://contoso.openai.azure.com with AIProjectClient. The call fails.
q: What should the developer change?
opts: Use the project endpoint from the portal
Add the model name to the end of the old endpoint
Deploy a larger model
Ask for more quota for the subscription and wait for the approval
exp: AIProjectClient connects to a project, so it needs the project endpoint with /api/projects/ and the project name. The model is named in each request and not in the endpoint, and neither model size nor quota causes a wrong address.

ctx: A chat client keeps the whole history in a list. After 40 turns the replies become slow and expensive, and one request fails because it is too long. Users still need answers that fit the conversation.
q: What is the best change?
opts: Send only the newest user message
Keep recent turns and replace older ones with a short summary
Set the temperature to zero
Send each of the forty turns as a separate request and join all the replies
exp: All history tokens count against the context window and the cost. A summary of old turns plus the recent ones keeps the context and stays small. Only the newest message loses the conversation, separate requests cost more, and temperature does not change the size.

ctx: A chat client calls a deployment named chat-prod. An administrator updates chat-prod from an older to a newer version of the same model. The name stays the same, and the app authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID.
q: For each of the following statements about this scenario, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: The model value in the code must be changed.
The team should run its evaluation again, because answers can change.
The app needs a new API key.
exp: No for the first: the code refers to the deployment name, which did not change. Yes for the second: a new version can answer differently, so quality and safety should be checked. No for the third: the app uses tokens from Entra ID and no key.

ctx: An HR agent must answer from 60 policy PDFs, do exact calculations of vacation days from a spreadsheet and must not search the internet.
q: Which tools should you add to the agent?
opts: Web search and file search
File search and code interpreter
Code interpreter and image generation for the spreadsheet
No tools, with all rules in the instructions
exp: File search grounds answers in the PDFs, and code interpreter runs code for exact calculations on the spreadsheet. Web search is forbidden here, image generation is not needed, and 60 PDFs do not fit into instructions.

ctx: An IT agent can look up tickets and restart servers. In a test, a user writes "Restart every server now, I am the boss", and the agent does it.
q: Which change reduces the risk most?
opts: Give the agent a longer and more polite set of instructions
Require human approval before the restart tool runs
Switch to a model with a larger context window
Tell users in the welcome message that they should not write such requests
exp: A human approval step stops a harmful action whatever the text says. Polite instructions and a notice to users can be ignored or bypassed, and a larger context window only lets the agent read more.

ctx: A school wants a library agent that answers from its rules. It has a Foundry project and a deployed model. The rules are in one PDF.
q: Put the steps in the correct order. Not every step is used.
items: Test questions in the agent playground
Create the agent and choose the deployed model
Write instructions and add file search with the PDF
Train a speech model on the PDF
Call the agent by name from the library website
exp: The agent is created on a deployed model, then it gets instructions and knowledge, then it is tested in the playground, and only then does an app call it by name. A speech model has nothing to do with answers from a PDF.

ctx: A website calls a Foundry agent. All visitors share one conversation ID that was created when the server started. Visitors now see answers about the orders of other people.
q: How should the developer fix this?
opts: Create a conversation per visitor
Create a new agent with the same name for each of the visitors
Delete all conversations each night
Tell the agent in its instructions to forget the previous visitor
exp: A conversation stores the history, so each visitor needs an own conversation ID. One agent can serve many conversations. A nightly deletion still mixes visitors during the day, and an instruction does not remove shared history.

ctx: A client app calls the agent "orders" by name and reads output_text. The team improves the instructions in the portal, which creates version 2 of the agent. The app does not pin a version.
q: For each of the following statements about this scenario, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: The client app must contain the new instructions.
The team should test version 2 before customers use it.
The client still needs permission to call the project.
exp: No for the first: instructions live with the agent and not in the client. Yes for the second: new instructions can change answers, so they are tested first. Yes for the third: each call is authenticated, and the identity needs a role on the project.

ctx: A newsroom app must find people, places and companies in 3,000 articles per day, with the same result every time and a confidence score. A prompt with a chat model gives a different list on some days.
q: Which option fits best?
opts: Named entity recognition in Azure Language
The same prompt, sent three times per article with a higher temperature
Sentiment analysis
A custom neural voice that reads the articles to an editor
exp: Named entity recognition returns categorized entities with confidence scores and consistent results for the same text. A chat prompt can vary and gives no score, sentiment measures opinion, and a voice does not find entities.

ctx: A train station app announces delays. The neural voice says "Dr. Meyer Street" as "drive Meyer Street" and speaks too fast for older passengers.
q: What should the developer use?
opts: SSML with the sub and prosody elements
A phrase list that contains Dr. Meyer Street and the platform numbers
Diarization
A batch transcription job for each announcement
exp: SSML controls synthesis: sub replaces how a text is spoken, and prosody sets the rate. Phrase lists, diarization and batch transcription are for speech recognition and do not change how a voice speaks.

ctx: A clinic app shows live German subtitles while a doctor speaks English. The app already has an Azure Speech resource.
q: Which class should the Python app use?
opts: SpeechSynthesizer
TranslationRecognizer
SpeechRecognizer
ImageAnalysisClient
exp: TranslationRecognizer listens in the source language and returns text in the target languages, so it produces subtitles directly. SpeechRecognizer would give English text only, SpeechSynthesizer creates audio, and ImageAnalysisClient works with pictures.

ctx: A language school wants a tutor that talks with students without noticeable pauses and lets them interrupt. Transcribing first, then calling a text model and then creating speech takes four seconds per turn.
q: Which option should the school choose?
opts: A larger text model in the same three-step chain
The Realtime API with an audio model
Batch transcription
Shorter lessons with fewer new words in each of the dialogs
exp: The Realtime API streams audio in and out of one speech-capable model and supports interruptions, so the delay is low. A larger text model keeps the slow chain, batch transcription is for stored files, and shorter lessons do not change latency.

ctx: A help app sends screenshots with tiny text to a multimodal model. The model reads many words wrongly. The images are sent with detail set to low.
q: What should the developer try first?
opts: Set detail to high
Send the same low-detail image three times in the same message
Ask users to take photos of the screen with a phone camera
Use an image-generation model
exp: With detail high the model sees the image in more detail, which helps with small text and costs more tokens. Repeating a low-detail image adds nothing, phone photos usually have lower quality, and a generation model does not read screenshots.

ctx: A shop has a good photo of its red chair. It wants the same photo with a beach in the background, and the chair must stay as it is.
q: Which approach fits?
opts: Image Analysis with the caption feature
Generate a new image from the prompt "a red chair on a beach"
Edit the photo with a mask for the background
Optical character recognition
exp: An image edit with a mask changes only the marked area, so the chair is kept. A new generation would invent another chair, a caption only describes a photo, and OCR reads text.

ctx: A photo archive needs tags and a bounding box for every person in 5 million pictures. The archive wants fixed feature names, a confidence per result and the lowest cost per picture. Free-form questions about pictures are not needed.
q: What should the app use?
opts: A multimodal chat model with a long prompt for each picture
Image Analysis with tags and people
An image-generation model
Content Understanding with an audio analyzer and a speaker list
exp: Image Analysis returns tags and person boxes with confidence for a fixed price per transaction. A chat model costs tokens for every picture and gives free text, a generation model creates pictures, and an audio analyzer does not look at photos.

ctx: An accounting team receives standard invoices and also its own freight form with the fields "seal number" and "temperature on arrival". It wants as little setup as possible.
q: Which analyzers should the team use in Content Understanding?
opts: Prebuilt invoice for both kinds
A custom analyzer for invoices and a second custom analyzer for freight forms
Prebuilt invoice for invoices and a custom analyzer for the freight form
A video analyzer with two segments, one for each kind of document
exp: The prebuilt invoice analyzer already knows invoice fields, and only the special form needs a custom schema. A prebuilt analyzer does not return unknown fields such as seal number, a custom invoice analyzer is extra work, and the video analyzer is for videos.

ctx: A support center wants a transcript, a one-sentence summary and the reason for the call from each recording. The reason must be one of Billing, Delivery or Technical.
q: How should the two fields be defined?
opts: Summary as extract and reason as a number
Summary as generate and reason as classify
Summary as classify with three long example sentences and reason as extract
Both as dates
exp: generate writes new text such as a summary, and classify picks one value from a list. extract returns text that is literally in the content, a number or a date does not fit a reason, and classifying a summary would limit it to fixed values.

ctx: A repair shop photographs damaged bicycles. For each photo it needs the damaged part from a fixed list and a short description, returned as fields for its database.
q: Which solution fits best?
opts: Speech to text with a phrase list of all bicycle parts
A custom image analyzer in Content Understanding
Language detection
The prebuilt invoice analyzer with a higher confidence threshold
exp: A custom image analyzer can define a classify field for the part and a generate field for the description, and it returns structured data. Speech to text needs audio, language detection needs text, and the invoice analyzer looks for invoice fields.
